transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-06-25 15:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ethan (CS), Aisha (Meadowlane CISO), Daniel (Head of Platform), Lena (Compliance), Ravi (DevOps)

Summary (auto):
Redwood gave an overview of data handling controls and confirmed that customer prompts/content are not used to train Redwood's models. Discussed encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options for private deployments, RBAC and SSO, audit logging retention, and data residency. Customer requested SOC2, sample logs, and a demo of key rotation.

Topics: prompt retention, PII/PHI, no-training confirmation, KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, private deployment

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. I'll hand off to Sofia to kick off on the security side - uh - hi Sofia.
[00:12] Sofia: Hi, thanks Jordan. Quick agenda: we'll cover data retention, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and answer any specific compliance questions. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:24] Aisha: Thanks, yes we have a few specific asks - first and foremost we need confirmation that you do not train your models on our prompts or any customer content. We need that in writing for our privacy team.
[00:36] Jordan: Totally understood. Short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to improve or train our public models. There is a distinction between telemetry used for debugging and training; we do not feed customer content into model training pipelines. We'll send the formal language and the policy.
[00:52] Daniel: Is that for hosted as well as dedicated? We run a mix of workloads.
[00:58] Sofia: Good question. For Hosted API, we have explicit controls and our policy is the same: no customer data is used to train models. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data remains isolated; with Private you can run entirely in your VPC and bring-your-own-keys.
[01:14] Lena: When you say "do not use for training" - does that include derived telemetry like prompt tokens, generated completions, or embeddings?
[01:24] Sofia: We collect limited telemetry for service health and billing - token counts, error rates, latency. We do not surface raw prompts to training. If a cust-- if a customer opts into a feedback program we can use anonymized snippets but that requires explicit consent and legal agreement.
[01:38] Aisha: Okay, that helps. Next - retention. What's default retention for prompts and transcripts? Our policy requires max 30 days unless we have contractual need.
[01:50] Jordan: Default retention for hosted accounts is 90 days for full transcript artifacts; aggregated billing metrics are retained longer. But we have controls: you can opt into a shorter retention window or enable automatic redaction. For Dedicated/Private you can set the retention to meet your policy. We'll share the retention-config doc.
[02:06] Ravi: Do you have inline redaction of PII/PHI? We need to scrub or mask PHI before anything is stored.
[02:14] Sofia: We support PII redaction pipelines: pre-send client-side redaction is recommended, but we also provide server-side masking for common PHI patterns. It's not perfect regex, but we do have a PII detection tooling which flags and masks. For high-risk data we recommend Private with BYOK so nothing persists in our hosted stores.
[02:36] Daniel: About BYOK - how does key rotation work? We have quarterly rotation requirements and key separation for dev/prod.
[02:44] Sofia: For Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customers can use on-prem HSMs. We support key rotation semantics and we can demonstrate a rotation flow - no downtime for in-flight requests as long as you follow the key aliasing pattern. We'll demo this.
[03:05] Aisha: For hosted accounts - do you manage the keys? Are they shared? We need to know where the master key is and who has access.
[03:13] Jordan: For hosted, Redwood manages the encryption keys; data is encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys. Access is restricted to a small ops team and logged. For customers requiring full control, Dedicated with customer-managed keys or Private with BYOK is the route. We'll send a KMS architecture diagram.
[03:30] Lena: Audit logging -- can you provide immutable audit logs showing access to raw prompts and exports? We may need those for audits.
[03:38] Sofia: Yes, we provide detailed audit logs for admin actions, API key usage, model deploys and data exports. Logs include timestamps, actor, action, resource. For Hosted we retain logs for 12 months by default; we can extend or provide exports. For Private you control log retention and storage.
[03:58] Ravi: Is the audit log tamperproof? Do you support log shipping to customer S3 or SIEM?
[04:04] Sofia: We support streaming logs to customer S3, Splunk, Datadog -- and we can provide signed logs or append-only store options for compliance.
[04:16] Aisha: Data residency -- our data must stay in US East region. Do you have region controls?
[04:22] Jordan: Yes, we have region controls. Hosted customers can choose region; Dedicated/Private give you more strict isolation. We'll confirm our region list and provide a data residency statement.
[04:34] Daniel: A few technical follow-ups - caching and KV caches, do those cache prompt content in memory or on disk? Could that count as retention?
[04:44] Sofia: Our runtime uses KV caches for attention state -- ephemeral in-memory caches that are not persisted to disk. They may be backed to local SSD under some configs but are encrypted and ephemeral. For customers concerned about any persistence, Private deployment with strict local policy can avoid disk writebacks.
[05:02] Aisha: Can you confirm you do not use our data to improve model weights, and will that be included in the contract?
[05:10] Jordan: Yes, we will include the "no-training" attestation clause in the contract language. I'll send the exact statutory wording from legal.
[05:18] Lena: Does Redwood ever share de-identified logs with third parties?
[05:22] Sofia: No, we do not share customer logs with third parties unless explicitly contracted or required by law. Aggregated telemetry might be published in aggregate, but nothing that could identify a customer.
[05:34] Ethan: Quick note, sometimes automated transcripts can mislabel things - the official artifacts we send are human-audited for enterprise accounts.
[05:42] Aisha: Good. About SSO -- we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Can you integrate with our SSO, enforce SCIM provisioning and role-based access control?
[05:52] Jordan: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Role-based access control supports custom roles and least-privilege. We'll share a mapping doc and offer a 1-hr setup session.
[06:04] Daniel: Are admin actions logged with the user email and IP? We need full audit trails.
[06:10] Sofia: Yes, audit logs include user identity, IP, timestamp and action. For elevated actions we log before/after states.
[06:18] Ravi: For HIPAA workloads, do you sign BAAs?
[06:22] Jordan: We do offer BAAs for enterprise customers under Private or Dedicated deployments. We'll include BAA process info in the follow-up.
[06:30] Aisha: On data retention detail - you mentioned default 90 days for hosted. Can you show how to programmatically purge or redact data sooner?
[06:40] Sofia: We have APIs for data deletion and a self-service retention setting per project. There's also a purge API that removes stored artifacts; for Hosted accounts, deletion requests are queued and we provide confirmation when complete. We'll include the API spec.
[06:54] Aisha: Great. For prompt redaction, what about free text embeddings? We plan to embed PHI fields in some flows.
[07:02] Sofia: Embeddings are treated like other content. If you send embeddings to our Hosted API they are persisted per retention policy. For PHI we recommend pre-hash or tokenization on client side or use Private deployment.
[07:18] Daniel: Any chance of accidental training via telemetry? Like if the telemetry pipeline writes samples to S3 that are later used for research?
[07:26] Jordan: We have strict separation -- telemetry storage is separate from our research/training datasets and access controls prevent that cross-use. This is part of our internal control and SOC2 scope. We'll send the control descriptions.
[07:38] Aisha: Requests for written artifacts: SOC 2 Type II, ISO certs, data retention policy, KMS integration guide, sample audit log.
[07:48] Jordan: We'll package and share those.
[07:52] Lena: One more -- do you ever use customer data for safety or moderation model improvement?
[07:58] Sofia: Safety signals might be used in aggregate to identify abusive patterns, but we do not tie specific customer content to model training. We can provide the boundary definitions.
[08:10] Aisha: Ok, thanks. Can we talk about encryption in transit specifics? TLS versions, mTLS?
[08:16] Sofia: All traffic to our hosted endpoints uses TLS 1.2+ with recommended ciphers. For higher security we support mTLS for Dedicated and Private or mutual TLS in front of private endpoints.
[08:26] Ravi: For backups, are snapshots encrypted with customer keys?
[08:30] Sofia: Backups are encrypted at rest using KMS. For hosted, encryption keys are managed by Redwood; for BYOK we store snapshots encrypted with customer keys where applicable.
[08:40] Daniel: How about penetration testing and vuln disclosures? We'll want to coordinate.
[08:44] Jordan: We do annual pentests and vuln scanning, and we have a vulnerability disclosure program. We'll share the policy and POC for security requests.
[08:54] Aisha: On the contract front, can you add specific data residency clauses and retention penalties if contractual obligations are not met?
[09:02] Jordan: We can negotiate these terms on the enterprise contract. We'll have legal follow up and include the retention SLAs.
[09:10] Lena: Last question from me -- do you provide a console to redact or delete individual items for compliance requests (e.g. subject access requests)?
[09:18] Sofia: Yes, we provide tooling in the Console for data subject access requests: search by id, purge artifacts, and generate attestations. We'll share screenshots and API examples.
[09:30] Aisha: Thanks -- let's summarize next steps.
[09:34] Jordan: Sure - Action items: we'll send SOC2 and ISO certs, KMS integration guide, sample logs; Sofia to demo key rotation; customer to confirm retention window and provide sample log format.
[09:46] Daniel: We'll aim to get the sample logs to you by Tuesday.
[09:50] Jordan: Great. Any other open items?
[09:54] Lena: No, that's it. Thanks.
[09:58] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and the docs.
[10:02] Jordan: Thanks everyone -- meeting closed.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional crosstalk, minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., KMS pronounced as K-M-S, sometimes "KV cache" becomes "K V cache"). References shared: SOC2 report (link: https://redwood.example/soc2), KMS integration guide (link: https://redwood.example/kms-guide), retention-config doc (link: https://redwood.example/retention).

End of transcript.
